previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a five-day history of non-bloody diarrhea, nausea, and epigastric pain, following an ER visit where creatinine was transiently elevated but returned to baseline. She is immunocompromised due to kidney transplant and on tacrolimus and sirolimus, which remained therapeutic throughout. Initial concern for C. difficile infection led to empiric vancomycin, but PCR testing was negative, and treatment was discontinued. Stool studies ruled out bacterial, parasitic, and viral pathogens. Abdominal pain persisted, prompting GI consultation; H. pylori was negative, and she was transitioned from famotidine to pantoprazole for empiric treatment of gastritis or peptic ulcer disease, with symptom improvement. On hospital day two, she developed dysuria; urinalysis showed infection, and culture grew E. coli, sensitive to multiple antibiotics. She was started on IV ceftriaxone and transitioned to oral cefpodoxime at discharge. Nausea resolved with ondansetron. She was discharged home with improved symptoms, instructions to continue transplant and blood pressure medications, and follow-up arranged with GI, transplant nephrology, and primary care.
